aspects.says: A generic override makes javac add a synthetic bridge method taking the erased type, with the method's annotations copied onto it, so a scan that does not skip isBridge() registers the method twice.
basis: section:The Compiler Adds Methods You Never Wrote: Bridges and Lambda Bodies

aspects.says: A lambda body becomes a private static synthetic method, and a narrower return type produces a bridge with the same name and parameters.
basis: section:The Compiler Adds Methods You Never Wrote: Bridges and Lambda Bodies
aspects.reason: two further shapes of the bridge rule that the page shows by listing; the subscriber practice and the quiz check bridges through a generic override, which is where scans go wrong

aspects.says: An object keeps no type arguments: an ArrayList<String> has the same Class as any ArrayList, and getGenericSuperclass() on it gives the class's declaration, AbstractList<E>.
basis: section:Type Arguments Survive in Declarations, Not in Objects

aspects.says: getDeclaredMethods() and getMethods() return members in no specified order, and the order changes with JVM setup even for the same class file and JDK.
basis: section:Reflection Returns Members in No Particular Order

aspects.says: getPermittedSubclasses() lists only direct subtypes, in no specified order, and returns null for a type that is not sealed, so nested sealed families need a recursive walk.
basis: section:Read a Record Through Its Components and a Sealed Type Through Its Permitted Subclasses

aspects.says: A permitted subclass that cannot be loaded is silently left out of getPermittedSubclasses().
basis: section:Read a Record Through Its Components and a Sealed Type Through Its Permitted Subclasses

aspects.says: getMethods() lists public methods including inherited ones; getDeclaredMethods() lists the class's own methods of every access level and nothing inherited.
basis: section:getMethods and getDeclaredMethods Answer Different Questions, and Neither Lists Everything

aspects.says: getRecordComponents() returns exactly a record's components in header order, while a method scan also finds toString and hashCode.
basis: section:Read a Record Through Its Components and a Sealed Type Through Its Permitted Subclasses

aspects.says: A class that extends a parameterized type keeps the type argument in its superclass signature, which getGenericSuperclass() reads back.
basis: section:Type Arguments Survive in Declarations, Not in Objects

aspects.says: Type arguments are kept in the generic signatures of fields, methods and classes and read with getGenericType() and its relatives, so a binder learns a list's element type from the declaration.
basis: section:Type Arguments Survive in Declarations, Not in Objects

aspects.says: Seeing every method of a type whatever its access takes getDeclaredMethods() on the class and on each getSuperclass() until it returns null.
basis: section:getMethods and getDeclaredMethods Answer Different Questions, and Neither Lists Everything
